disease_label_per_paper: Fulminant hepatitis A and E co-infection leading to acute liver failure
presentation_summary: 38-year-old Asian man presented with two weeks of abdominal discomfort, lethargy, and jaundice.
Two days before emergency presentation he developed altered mental status and disorientation to time and space.
Exam showed severe jaundice, yellow sclera and skin, abdominal tenderness, palpable liver, grade 2 hepatic encephalopathy, confusion, and GCS 10.

Admission labs showed AST 2100 U/L, ALT 2200 U/L, total bilirubin 28 mg/dL, INR 2.4, ammonia 59 umol/L, WBC 18 x10^9/L, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, sodium 128 mEq/L, potassium 3.2 mEq/L, and fasting glucose 75 mg/dL.

The patient was treated in ICU with supportive care, ribavirin for active HEV replication context, lactulose, electrolyte/glucose correction, mannitol for increased intracranial pressure, dialysis after deterioration, and transplant-center referral, but died within 48 hours because no donor was available.
